title: When the Provision Sings
premise: Oscar Lockridge has spent seven years outrunning a manslaughter charge and his own grief, ferrying supplies to river settlements where no one asks questions. When floodwater exposes the chest of the Meridian, a salvage ship that sank with a nation's treasury aboard, Oscar's discovery makes him the most wanted man on the water — hunted by a salvage fleet captain who once loved him and an heir whose claim could redeem or destroy him. Racing six tides to reach the wreck first, Oscar must choose between the clean escape he's always planned and the people worth stopping for. He reaches the wreck, loses the treasure to the river itself, and gains something rarer: a verdict of his own making.
about_author: Q. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former bush-strip mechanic who spent four seasons along remote northern waterways before turning to fiction. Their work explores what survival costs the people who are good at it.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A routine medicine run through fog ends with him crash-landing on a sandbar newly risen from floodwater, where he pries open a chest stamped with the seal of Meridia, a drowned nation-state. The beat: restless competence curdling into dread as he realizes some cargo can't be dropped off and forgotten.

chapters.title: The Six-Tide Clock
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the trading post of Kettle Landing, word travels faster than planes; within hours three parties want the chest — including Captain Ilsa Vane of the salvage fleet, the woman he abandoned years ago. He learns the wreck lies under shallows that close after six tides. Beat: the trap of being known.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Heir
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She charters Oscar at gunpoint-adjacent politeness, bringing aboard Tomas Reyes, last living claimant to the Meridian fortune, who insists the treasure belongs to the people it was stolen from, not the finders. Beat: uneasy alliance; love against duty begins its argument.

chapters.title: Rumors Weigh More Than Medicine
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Flying the river route, Oscar discovers every settlement already knows about the chest, and one village offers to hide him if he'll fly their sick girl out first — a detour that costs half a tide. Beat: the price of survival measured in someone else's life.

chapters.title: What Vane Keeps in Her Hold
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Aboard the fleet's lead ship, Tomas finds evidence Ilsa isn't hunting treasure but proof — her father died salvaging the Meridian, branded a thief. She needs the wreck's manifest to clear his name. Beat: enemies revealed as mirrors of Oscar's own flight from judgment.

chapters.title: The Storm That Settles Arguments
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A squall forces all three parties onto the same island overnight; knives come out over the chest until the storm nearly drowns them all, and Oscar saves Ilsa against his own interest. Beat: tenderness breaking through hostility, and the cost of caring made physical.

chapters.title: Two Tides Short
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. With two tides left, Oscar's plane is sabotaged by a rival crewman; grounded, they must take the slow river route, and Tomas confesses the 'heir' story is partly invented — he's the heir's archivist, carrying a dead man's claim. Beat: betrayal, then forgiveness offered anyway.

chapters.title: The Wreck Sings
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At slack water they dive the Meridian and find not gold but sealed state records — the treasury was a lie, the ship carried evidence of the nation's own crimes. The rival fleet arrives armed. Beat: awe and horror; the inheritance is guilt, not wealth.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. As the channel closes, Oscar chooses to sink the records' location with the wreck rather than let any faction own them, broadcasting copies instead to every settlement radio — justice by rumor, the only currency the interior trusts. Beat: sacrifice of escape for accountability.

chapters.title: Where the River Lets You Land
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Oscar turns himself in on the old charge; Isla testifies, Tomas publishes the truth, and the settlements remember the pilot who stopped moving. Released to community service flying medevac, Oscar lands without running. Beat: stillness earned; the provision finally sings quiet.
